oligos.sugar_modifications: LNA at upper-case positions, DNA at lower-case positions, per the source's stated case legend '(uppercase LNA, lowercase DNA)'. No 2'-MOE / 2'-OMe / 2'-F is mentioned anywhere in the source.
oligos.gapmer_design: 3-8-3 LNA-DNA-LNA gapmer read off the printed case convention (positions 1-3 LNA, 4-11 DNA, 12-14 LNA). The source does not itself use the word 'gapmer' or print a design string.
oligos.notes: Source: 'Targets the proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) mRNA ... It matches the sequence of humans and cynomolgus monkeys and has a single, end-standing mismatch to the minipig sequence.' The '(uppercase LNA, lowercase DNA)' legend is printed on THIS compound and is the legend applied to all four sequences. Primes are the typographic U+2032 character, as printed. Source states for all four compounds: 'LNA SSO formulations contained ≤7% impurities, and the presence of endotoxins was excluded.' No purity assay, identity check or synthesis platform is named beyond 'synthesized according to standard protocols as previously described (Lindholm et al., 2012; Straarup et al., 2010), were characterized'.

measurements.source_locus: RESULTS > 'In-Life Observations and Clinical Pathology' > RTR5001 paragraph, sentence 1; corroborated by Table 1 row 'Coagulation', RTR5001 minipig cell ('–')
measurements.verbatim_quote: There were no RTR5001-related clinical signs or ISRs and no change in hematology, coagulation parameters and cytokines was observed.
measurements.notes: MEASURED NULL (absence row), not silence: the coagulation panel was run (Methods: 'Blood was sampled on different occasions for assessment of a full set of hematology, coagulation, and clinical chemistry parameters', ACL TOP500 analyser) and is reported as unchanged. The source writes 'coagulation parameters' as a composite and does not name the analytes here; elsewhere in this paper the reported coagulation analytes are PT, APTT and fibrinogen. I deliberately did NOT split this into per-analyte PT/APTT/fibrinogen rows, because the source does not name them in this sentence. Table 1's Coagulation cell for RTR5001 minipig is an en dash; the table writes 'Not examined' explicitly where a parameter was not assessed, so the dash means assessed-and-no-finding.

measurements.verbatim_quote: Neutrophil (2-fold) and monocyte (2.7-fold) counts as well as fibrinogen (2.2-fold) levels were significantly (P < .001) increased in minipigs at 24 mg/kg on day 17.
measurements.notes: The 2.2-fold figure is the fibrinogen value; the 2-fold and 2.7-fold figures in the same sentence are neutrophils and monocytes and are NOT coagulation readouts - do not mis-map them. Fibrinogen rose alongside neutrophilia and monocytosis, which reads like an acute-phase response rather than a clotting defect, but the source does not label it either way and no interpretation is added here. Absolute fibrinogen concentrations and units are never printed - only the fold change. Nothing reported at 8 mg/kg.

measurements.notes: BLEEDING TIED TO THE COAGULATION CASCADE BY THE SOURCE ITSELF: the very next sentence begins 'Accordingly, transient and statistically significant increases in PT and APTT were observed at 45 mg/kg', and the Discussion groups them - 'Corresponding clinical signs, including prolonged bleeding and red discoloration of parts of the body, were also transient and reversed within a few minutes after administration.' DOSE ATTRIBUTION CAVEAT: this sentence does not itself restate a dose; 45 mg/kg is taken from the immediately preceding sentence, 'After repeated dosing, the majority of minipigs dosed at 45 mg/kg presented with a transient flushing of limbs, ears and nose immediately after dosing.' No formal bleeding-time assay (e.g. template bleeding time in minutes) was performed - this is an observation at venipuncture, so no value or unit exists. No animal count is given.

measurements.notes: REPORTING SILENCE, not a measured null, and the most consequential gap in this bundle. Fibrinogen is reported for RTR4955 in this same paper, so it was in the coagulation panel, yet no fibrinogen result is given for RTR2996 - the compound with by far the largest clotting-time signal (about 3.5-fold PT/APTT). Without fibrinogen, a consumptive coagulopathy cannot be separated from the classic phosphorothioate plasma-protein-binding / ex vivo assay artefact using this source alone.

The cell for this compound/species is a single en dash (U+2013), which is what verbatim_quote holds - it is the exact and complete cell content, but on its own it proves little, so here is the whole Table 1 'Coagulation' row in printed column order with cell boundaries marked by ' | ' (the pipes are added by me, they are not in the source): Coagulation | – | – | ↑ Fibrinogen at 24 mg/kg | ↑ Fibrinogen at ≥8 mg/kg | ↑ PT and APTT at ≥ 12 mg/kg | ↑ PT and APTT at ≥ 12 mg/kg | ↑ PT and APTT at 45 mg/kg associated with flushing of limbs, ear and nose | ↑ PT and APTT at ≥ 20 mg/kg . Table 1 writes 'Not examined' in words where a parameter was not assessed (e.g. 'Exposure Kidney cortex' for RTR2996 NHP; 'Lymph nodes' for RTR3649 minipig), so a dash means assessed with no finding. Recorded as a measured null on that convention. No analyte names, values or n are given.

extraction_notes: SCOPE: one source (S1), four LNA phosphorothioate single-stranded oligonucleotides, two species (Goettingen minipig as primary data, NHP as a summary column), 23 coagulation rows.  (1) BUNDLE BRIEF IS WRONG ABOUT THE COMPOUND COUNT. The brief promised '5 named LNA oligos with PRINTED SEQUENCES'. The paper names and prints sequences for FOUR: RTR5001, RTR4955, RTR3649, RTR2996. Occurrence counts across the XML are RTR4955 x54, RTR5001 x53, RTR2996 x41, RTR3649 x29 and RTR2966 x1. The single 'RTR2966' is a typographical error for RTR2996 inside Methods > 'Exposure Assessment' ('for RTR2966 up until 48 h after the first and last doses'); there is no fifth compound, no fifth sequence and no fifth study. This also resolves the triage note that two sweeps 'disagreed on the compound list (RTR2966 vs RTR4955/RTR5001 emphasis)' - the disagreement was an artefact of that typo.  (2) DOI MISMATCH IN THE BUNDLE METADATA. The brief gives 10.1093/toxsci/kfw249. The article's own <article-id pub-id-type="doi"> is 10.1093/toxsci/kfx025. PMID 28123102 and PMC5414856 both match. The file's DOI was recorded; the brief's DOI should be corrected upstream.  (3) FIGURE 4A WAS NOT DIGITISED. Figure 4A is the only place the RTR2996 PT/APTT time course at 0, 5, 15 and 45 mg/kg exists as numbers. Per instruction, nothing was read off the plot. Eight rows (RTR2996 PT/APTT after the first dose, at 24 h, and at 5/15 mg/kg) therefore carry readout_value NOT_REPORTED with readout_is_qualitative true. The only coagulation numbers anywhere in the text are: fibrinogen 2.2-fold (RTR4955), PT 10-26% and APTT up to 18% (RTR3649), and 'about 3.5 fold' for PT and APTT jointly (RTR2996 after the last dose). No absolute clotting time in seconds and no absolute fibrinogen concentration is printed anywhere in this paper.  (4) THE 'ABOUT 3.5 FOLD' IS SHARED BETWEEN TWO ANALYTES. The source writes 'increases in PT and APTT ... became more pronounced after the last dose (mean values were about 3.5 fold higher than baseline)'. It gives one number for both analytes. Two rows carry it (PT and aPTT) and both say so in notes; they are not independent measurements and must not be averaged or treated as two observations.  (5) TABLE 1 DASH CONVENTION. Table 1 uses an en dash for 'assessed, nothing found' and the words 'Not examined' where a parameter was not assessed (e.g. 'Exposure Kidney cortex' for RTR2996 NHP, 'Lymph nodes' for RTR3649 minipig). Dashes were therefore read as measured nulls, not as missing data. Only two rows in this bundle use effect_direction 'no_change': RTR5001 minipig (backed by an explicit narrative sentence) and RTR5001 NHP (backed by the dash convention).  (6) THE NHP COLUMN IS SECONDARY DATA. All six monkey rows come from the NHP half of Table 1, which the table header attributes to earlier studies (Gebert et al., 2014; Hildebrandt-Eriksen et al., 2012; Koch and Orum, 2008; Lindholm et al., 2012) plus 'data on file, F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd., 2017'. No n, no timepoints, no magnitudes, no statistics. They are flagged SECONDARY DATA in every notes field and should not be pooled with the primary minipig rows.  (7) CROSS-SPECIES DOSES ARE NOT COMPARABLE FOR RTR2996. Minipig dose levels were 0/5/15/45 mg/kg i.v. and NHP 0/3/20/60 mg/kg i.v.; Methods state 'The RT2996 dose levels for the minipig were reduced by 1/3 compared to NHP, aiming for comparable liver exposures'. The minipig 45 mg/kg threshold and the NHP >=20 mg/kg threshold cannot be compared on a mg/kg basis. Route also differs for RTR3649 (minipig s.c., NHP i.v.).  (8) A CONTRADICTION INSIDE THE SOURCE (not a coagulation row, but it shows Table 1 is not reliable standalone). For RTR2996 at 45 mg/kg the Results text says 'A reduction in red blood cell (RBC; 11%) and lymphocyte counts (35%) and an increase in reticulocyte count (2.2-fold) were also observed', while Table 1's Hematology cell says 'Rbc, lymphocytes and reticulocytes' all DECREASED. The direction of the reticulocyte change is contradictory between narrative and table. Wherever narrative and Table 1 both cover a coagulation readout here they agree, but any future extraction should prefer the narrative.  (9) SEQUENCE CHEMISTRY AND THE CASE LEGEND. The legend '(uppercase LNA, lowercase DNA)' is printed exactly once, parenthetically after the RTR5001 sequence, and is applied here to all four sequences printed in the same Methods paragraph. This is stated in every modifications 'basis' field and in each oligo's notes. All 57 modification rows were machine-checked: contiguous 1..N, nucleobase identical to the sequence at that position. backbone_linkage_3p is PS for positions 1..N-1 and NOT_APPLICABLE at the 3'-terminal position, from 'phosphorothioated LNA-based SSOs'; the source never counts the linkages, so ps_count is NOT_REPORTED. is_5_methyl_C is false everywhere, meaning NOT STATED BY THE SOURCE - it is not an affirmative claim that the cytosines are unmethylated. RTR3649's printed sequence carries a stray acute accent after the 3' prime, a typesetting artefact.  (10) ALIASES DELIBERATELY LEFT NOT_REPORTED. The source prints only the RTRxxxx codes. The sequences are recognisable to anyone who works on this compound class, but mapping them to any other development code would be an inference from outside this document, so aliases are NOT_REPORTED for all four. Map them downstream against a source that actually prints the correspondence.  (11) COAGULATION ANALYTES NEVER MEASURED OR REPORTED IN THIS SOURCE. There is no TT, ACT, INR, D-dimer, antithrombin, anti-Xa, anti-IIa, thrombin generation (ETP or peak), prekallikrein, or individual factor activity (FVII, FXI, FXII) anywhere in the paper, for any compound or species. The entire coagulation dataset is PT, APTT and fibrinogen plus one observational bleeding note. This is study-level reporting silence and is recorded here rather than as 20+ empty rows.  (12) PLATELETS. The word 'thrombocytopenia' appears exactly once, in the Introduction, as a general statement about the compound class citing other authors. No platelet count is reported for any dose group in this study, and nothing ties platelets to a coagulation-cascade readout. No platelet row was extracted, consistent with the instruction that platelet count alone is a different endpoint.  (13) COMPLEMENT IS ADJACENT BUT OUT OF SCOPE. CH50 is co-reported with coagulation in the same figure (Figure 4B) and the same paragraph, and the Discussion links flushing to complement activation at a plasma Cmax of approximately 500 microgram/mL RTR2996 versus a reported NHP threshold of 70-80 microgram/mL. Complement is not a coagulation-cascade readout and no complement row was written; noted here because a reviewer will see the two effects reported together.  (14) NON-STANDARD readout_unit VALUE. Two rows use '%_change_vs_control', which is not in the contract's suggested unit list. It is used deliberately: the source prints the SIZE OF THE INCREASE (PT '10-26%', APTT 'up to 18%'), which is neither '%_of_control' nor 'fold_change'. Recording these as '%_of_control' would invert their meaning (a 10% increase is 110% of control). The APTT value is stored as the string 'up to 18' because the source gives an upper bound, not a point estimate.  (15) QUOTE FIDELITY AND VERIFICATION METHOD. The JATS XML is effectively one line, so quotes were taken from a parsed, tag-stripped rendering: inline markup (<italic>, <bold>, <underline>) removed, entity references decoded (< -> '<'), and thin spaces (U+2009) and non-breaking spaces collapsed to single ASCII spaces. Typographic characters that carry meaning are preserved verbatim: en dash in '10-26%' is U+2013, '>=' signs are U+2265, up arrows are U+2191, primes are U+2032. Verification was two-tier and every row passed: the 16 narrative- and figure-legend-derived quotes were programmatically re-checked to occur in that normalised running text, and the 7 Table 1-derived quotes were re-checked against the exact parsed content of the table's <td> elements. The four printed sequences were checked against the running text and all four passed. SEPARATE PARSING HAZARD: when the tags are stripped, adjacent table cells concatenate with NO separator - the Coagulation row flattens to 'Coagulation--↑ Fibrinogen at 24 mg/kg↑ Fibrinogen at ≥8 mg/kg↑ PT and APTT at ≥ 12 mg/kg...' - so the staged flattened files PMC5414856.txt and MINIPIG_PMC5414856.txt cannot be used to read Table 1 reliably and were not used for it. A second hazard in the same table: the 'Additional organs' row starts with three EMPTY <td> cells, so any flattened read of that row shifts its content leftwards into the wrong compound's column.  (16) ON-TARGET VS UNINTENDED. None of the four targets (PCSK9, APOB, miR-122, BCL2) is a coagulation gene, so on_target_effect is false on every row. The source attributes the cholesterol / LDL / HDL / triglyceride changes to 'expected pharmacologic effects' and never attributes any coagulation change to pharmacology. unintended_toxicity is true on the rows reporting an effect and false on the null and silence rows.  (17) GROUP SIZES. Minipig groups were n=3 per dose except RTR2996 at 45 mg/kg, which had 5 animals (3 main study plus 2 assigned to recovery) - consistent with 'One of the five minipigs at 45 mg/kg' and the Figure 4 legend 'N = 3 or N = 5'. Controls: 2 PBS (RTR5001, RTR4955) and 3 saline (RTR3649, RTR2996). One RTR4955 animal at 24 mg/kg was killed on day 15, i.e. before the day-17 fibrinogen sampling that its dose group's value is drawn from.  (18) SUPPLEMENTARY DATA. The paper cites 'Supplementary data are available at Toxicological Sciences online'. That file is not staged in /home/user/coag-staging/fulltext and was not consulted; if it contains the Figure 4A source values, it would convert eight qualitative rows into numeric ones.
refused_rows: (A) FIGURE 4A PER-TIMEPOINT PT/APTT VALUES (RTR2996, 0/5/15/45 mg/kg, predose through day 15 with post-dose hours). Plainly extractable by pixel measurement and would have been the single richest yield in this bundle - roughly 8 timepoints x 4 dose groups x 2 analytes. Refused: reading numbers off a plotted panel is prohibited, and nothing in the text gives these values. Recorded instead as NOT_REPORTED / qualitative rows so the gap is visible.  (B) FIGURE 4B CH50 COMPLEMENT VALUES. Figure-only and outside the coagulation endpoint. Refused on both counts.  (C) INJECTION-SITE HAEMORRHAGES (Table 1, row 's.c. injection sites': RTR5001 minipig and NHP 'inflammation, necrosis and/or edema, hemorrhages'; RTR4955 minipig 'Increased severity and incidence of hemorrhages'; RTR3649 minipig 'increased hemorrhage and fibroplasia at 48 mg/kg'). These are local reactions at a subcutaneous injection site, described by the source as part of an inflammatory injection-site reaction. The source never links them to a clotting defect, and the two compounds involved showed either no coagulation finding at all (RTR5001) or raised fibrinogen in the procoagulant direction (RTR4955). Filing them as bleeding_outcome rows would manufacture a coagulopathy signal the source does not support.  (D) VISCERAL HAEMORRHAGES IN THE NHP RTR4955 STUDY: Table 1, row 'Additional organs', 'hemorrhages in cecum, colon and lung at >= 8 mg/kg', and Table 1, row 'Mortality', '1 humane killed at 24 mg/kg with hemorrhages, edema and necrosis of cecum, incl. liver and kidney changes'. This is the closest call in the bundle. Refused because the source presents both as histopathological findings within a gastrointestinal / hepatic / renal toxicity, never attributes them to a coagulation defect, and reports no clotting-time abnormality for RTR4955 in either species - its only coagulation finding is INCREASED fibrinogen. PARSING HAZARD WORTH RECORDING: the 'Additional organs' row is sparse (three empty <td> cells before the first populated one), so a flattened-text read of that row silently shifts the cells one or more columns left and can attribute this haemorrhage finding to the RTR4955 MINIPIG or even to RTR5001. The raw table markup was inspected to confirm it is the 4th data cell, i.e. RTR4955 NHP.  (E) PLATELET COUNTS. None are reported in this study for any group; the only platelet-adjacent word is 'thrombocytopenia' in a general Introduction sentence about the compound class, citing other authors. No row written - it is a different Challenge endpoint and there is no coagulation-cascade tie here.  (F) DISCUSSION SIMILARITY CLAIMS AS MEASUREMENTS, e.g. 'With the confirmed occurrence of acute PT and APTT prolongations after high intravenous doses in both species, this effect is likely also relevant in terms of human safety' and 'Effects on the coagulation, renal, and complement systems were also similar to those in NHPs.' These are the authors' interpretation across studies, not measurements with a dose, timepoint or value. Used only as corroboration inside notes fields.  (G) HUMAN OR CLINICAL COAGULATION DATA. The paper repeatedly mentions that these compounds were tested in humans and that clinical plasma peaks are 'often below NHP thresholds', but it reports no human coagulation measurement of its own. No clinical row was written.  (H) PER-DOSE OR PER-DAY SPLITS OF THE RTR3649 PT/APTT RANGES. '10-26%' and 'up to 18%' span 12 and 48 mg/kg and days 16, 25 and 30 collectively. Splitting them into six dose x day cells would have quadrupled the row count with invented precision. Kept as two rows with the combined dose and timepoint strings.
